info.title: Research Reader API
info.description:
Local-first bilingual research-paper reader.

This document is generated from the wire contract (ADR 0006) and the FastAPI application, so the schemas cannot drift from the code.

There is no authentication. The service binds loopback and refuses a state-changing request whose Origin or Referer is not local, which stops a page on another origin from making this service import, translate or delete. That is a browser-origin check and is not described as authentication.

get.description: Liveness plus what this server is actually able to do.

post.description:
Import a file.

The upload is streamed to disk and then identified from its own bytes; the declared filename
is a hint and never a fact about the content.  Deduplication is by content hash inside the
service — not by a key supplied here — so the same bytes cannot be stored twice even if a
caller sends a different key, and the parse job's idempotency key is derived from the
document and the hash rather than from the request.

delete.description:
Delete a document and everything derived from it.

``confirm=true`` is required: this removes the stored original as well as the parse, the
translations and the annotations, and there is no undo.

get.description: The stored original, byte for byte, exactly as imported.  Never rewritten.
One page with its blocks, their display-space spans and their chosen translations.
What translation would use.  The API key is reported as a boolean and never echoed.

schema.title: Response Translation Configuration Api V1 Translation Configuration Get

get.description:
Everything needed to render the settings panel, and nothing secret.

Reports the effective value, the stored value separately, and where the effective one came
from.  The stored value is separate on purpose: when the environment is overriding a stored
setting, the reader must be able to see the value they typed *and* the value in force, or
the panel looks broken.

schema.title: Response Get Translation Settings Api V1 Settings Translation Get

put.description: Store settings.  Takes effect on the next job; neither process needs restarting.

schema.title: Response Put Translation Settings Api V1 Settings Translation Put

delete.description: Forget every stored translation setting, falling back to the environment and defaults.

schema.title: Response Delete Translation Settings Api V1 Settings Translation Delete

post.description:
Send one real request with the settings currently in force and report what came back.

This is the only way to find out whether a base URL, a model id and a key work together,
and it is why this endpoint exists rather than leaving the reader to guess from job
failures.  It sends a few tokens to the configured service - that is a real outbound
request, and the caller is told so in the response.

Nothing is stored, cached or recorded: a check that writes a translation would poison the
cache with a fake unit.

schema.title: Response Test Translation Settings Api V1 Settings Translation Test Post

post.description:
Queue a translation job.

The job is planned before it is queued, so the response can state how many blocks would be
sent and how many are already cached.  Nothing is sent from this endpoint — a worker does
that — and the worker refuses an oversized plan before spending anything.

schema.title: Response List Translations Api V1 Documents  Document Id  Translations Get

patch.description:
Record a human correction.

A new row is written with ``origin='human'`` and a higher version instead of editing the
machine row, so machine output is never destroyed and the original row's cache key stays
meaningful.  The correction deliberately carries a cache key of its own, so it can never be
mistaken for reusable machine output.

Response Get Job Api V1 Jobs  Job Id  Get

get.description: Append-only events after ``since``, so a running job can be polled without re-fetching.

Response List Terms Api V1 Terms Get

post.description:
Add or update a glossary term.

Changing a term's target text bumps its ``version``, and the glossary version is part of the
translation cache key, so affected translations are re-requested rather than silently
reused.  The term's scope is derived from whether it names a document, which is what the
table's uniqueness constraint is built on.

schema.title: Response Delete Term Api V1 Terms  Term Id  Delete
Response Get Reading State Api V1 Documents  Document Id  Reading State Get

get.description:
Bilingual Markdown.

The file states in its own header that it is a reflowed transcript rather than a facsimile,
and that the anchoring is block-level.  Those claims travel with the file so that a reader
who only has the export still knows what it is.
